character.addNeedsOnline: Traits can only be changed while the player is online — the game needs the character loaded.
character.exclusionsHidden: Traits that clash with one the player already has are not offered.
character.jobTraitsHint: A profession grants exactly one of these. A character can only hold one profession — an extra profession trait is the only way to give them a second job’s benefits.
character.reconnectNotice: A changed trait takes effect on the server at once. The player only sees it in their own character sheet after reconnecting — the game does not transmit traits while play is running. That is also why the profession cannot be changed.

traitDescription.allthumbs:
Transfers inventory items slowly. Can't craft anything while walking.
Slower rope climbing speed, and higher chance of falling.
Slower weapon shouldering time.
traitDescription.artisan: Better at pottery and glass crafts.
traitDescription.athletic:
Faster running speed.
Can run for longer without tiring.
traitDescription.axeman:
Better at chopping trees.
Faster axe swing.
traitDescription.blacksmith: Can use an anvil to create metal items.
traitDescription.blacksmith2: Can use an anvil to create metal items.
traitDescription.burglar: Can hotwire vehicles. Less chance of breaking window locks.
traitDescription.claustrophobic: Gets panicked when in small indoor rooms.
traitDescription.conspicuous: More likely to be spotted by zombies.
traitDescription.crafty: Increased XP gains for Crafting skills.
traitDescription.desensitized:
Far less prone to panic.
Ignore discomfort.
traitDescription.dextrous:
Transfers inventory items quickly.
Faster rope climbing speed, and less chance of falling.
Faster weapon shouldering time.
traitDescription.disorganized:
Decreased container inventory capacity.
Affects world containers and bags, but not your main inventory.
traitDescription.eagleeyed:
Faster visibility fade.
Higher visibility arc.
Weapon sights more effective at long range.
traitDescription.emaciated: Low strength, low endurance and prone to injury.
traitDescription.fasthealer: Recovers quickly from injuries and illness.
traitDescription.fastreader: Takes less time to read books.
traitDescription.feeble:
Less knockback from melee weapons.
Decreased carrying weight.
traitDescription.hardofhearing:
Smaller perception radius.
Smaller hearing range.
traitDescription.hemophobic:
Panic when performing first aid on self.
Cannot perform first aid on others.
Gets stressed when bloody.
traitDescription.herbalist: Can find medicinal herbs and craft medicines and poultices from them.
traitDescription.herbalist_prof: Can find medicinal herbs and craft medicines and poultices from them.
traitDescription.illiterate: Cannot read any books or in-world text.
traitDescription.inconspicuous: Less likely to be spotted by zombies.
traitDescription.insomniac: Slow loss of tiredness while sleeping.
traitDescription.inventive: Has lower skill level requirements to research recipes from items or auto learn recipes.
traitDescription.inventive_prof: Has lower skill level requirements to research recipes from items or auto learn recipes.
traitDescription.irongut: Less chance to have food illness.
traitDescription.marksman:
Improved gun accuracy and damage.
Quicker reload.
traitDescription.mason: Better at building stone and brick constructions.
traitDescription.mechanics: Has knowledge of common and commercial vehicle models, and repairs.
traitDescription.mechanics2: Has knowledge of common and commercial vehicle models, and repairs.
traitDescription.nightowl:
Requires little sleep.
Stays extra alert even when sleeping.
traitDescription.nutritionist: Can see the nutritional values of any food.
traitDescription.nutritionist2: Can see the nutritional values of any food.
traitDescription.obese: Reduced running speed, very low endurance and prone to injury.
traitDescription.outdoorsman: Less affected by harsh weather conditions.
traitDescription.overweight: Reduced running speed, low endurance and prone to injury.
traitDescription.pronetoillness:
More prone to disease.
Faster rate of zombification.
traitDescription.resilient:
Less prone to disease.
Slower rate of zombification.
traitDescription.shortsighted:
Smaller view distance.
Slower visibility fade.
Weapon sights less effective.
traitDescription.slowhealer: Recovers slowly from injuries and illness.
traitDescription.slowreader: Takes longer to read books and other literature.
traitDescription.smoker:
Unhappiness rises when tobacco is not smoked.
Stress and unhappiness decrease after smoking tobacco.
traitDescription.stout:
Extra knockback from melee weapons.
Increased carrying weight.
traitDescription.strong:
Extra knockback from melee weapons.
Increased carrying weight.
traitDescription.thickskinned: Lower chance of being scratched or bitten.
traitDescription.thinskinned: Higher chance of being scratched or bitten by zombies.
traitDescription.underweight: Low strength, low endurance and prone to injury.
traitDescription.unfit: Very low endurance and endurance regeneration.
traitDescription.very underweight: Very low strength, very low endurance and prone to injury.
traitDescription.weak:
Far less knockback from melee weapons.
Extremely small carrying weight.
traitDescription.weakstomach: Higher chance to have food illness.
traitDescription.weightgain: Permanent tendency to gain weight. Starts with High Weight trait.
traitDescription.weightloss: Permanent tendency to lose weight. Starts with Low Weight trait.
traitDescription.whittler: Can carve wood and bone items.
traitDescription.wildernessknowledge:
Can find medicinal herbs and craft medicines and poultices from them, and make simple stone and bone tools.
Start fires faster.

credits.dataProtectionBody: The panel stores player names, SteamIDs, positions and skills, because a ban without a SteamID and a map without positions do not work. How long players nobody has seen are kept is the operator’s decision — the default is indefinitely.
credits.description: Where the artwork this panel shows comes from.

credits.tilesWhere: Road and grass tiles from the game's texture packs, as the ground under the vehicle preview.

credits.unofficial: This is an unofficial fan production for non-commercial purposes made under the Indie Stone Terms.

alarm.description: Sets off an alarm in the building an admin is standing in. With no admin in game, nothing happens.
alarm.title: Building alarm

broadcast.description: A message to everyone. It appears as a server message, not under a name.
broadcast.title: Broadcast

chopper.description: Starts the helicopter event. It pulls zombies from half the map.
chopper.title: Helicopter

generateWeather.description: Lets the weather simulation decide what arrives. A warm or cold front and its strength are what you give it.
generateWeather.title: Generate weather

gunshot.description: A shot near a random player. Zombies hear it from a long way off.
gunshot.title: Gunshot

hordeAtPoint.description: Puts zombies at a spot on the map. The area has to be loaded — a player must be nearby, otherwise the server answers “invalid location”.
hordeAtPoint.title: Horde at a point

hordeNearPlayer.description: Puts zombies around a player. They notice them at once.
hordeNearPlayer.title: Horde near a player

lightning.description: A lightning strike over a player. Left empty it picks a random one.
lightning.title: Lightning

releaseSnow.description: Lifts a pinned precipitation type so the game decides for itself whether it snows.
releaseSnow.title: Hand the snow back

releaseTemperature.description: Lifts a set temperature so the game runs the season's own again.
releaseTemperature.title: Hand the temperature back

removeZombies.description: Removes every loaded zombie within a radius of a point.
removeZombies.title: Remove zombies

setClouds.description: How heavily the sky is covered.
setClouds.title: Cloud cover

setDate.description: Sets the day and month. The season follows from it.
setDate.title: Set the date

setDaylight.description: How bright the day is. Below 100 the world turns gloomy.
setDaylight.title: Daylight

setFog.description: How thick the fog lies. 0 is clear, 100 is impenetrable.
setFog.title: Fog

setPower.description: Switches the electricity on or off. The game has no switch but a shut-off day — "on" sets it to never, "off" to today.
setPower.title: Power

setSnow.description: Whether precipitation falls as snow or as rain. The game refuses snow outside a cold season and names the temperature when it does.
setSnow.title: Precipitation type

setTemperature.description: The outdoor temperature in degrees Celsius.
setTemperature.title: Temperature

setTime.description: Sets the in-game clock. 0 is midnight, 12 is noon.
setTime.title: Set the time

setWater.description: Switches the water on or off, by the same route as the power.
setWater.title: Water

soundAtPlayer.description: Makes a noise where a player stands. Zombies walk towards it.
soundAtPlayer.title: Sound at a player

soundAtPoint.description: Makes a noise at a spot on the map. Zombies walk towards it.
soundAtPoint.title: Sound at a point

startBlizzard.description: Triggers the game's own winter storm, which sets the precipitation, the wind and the temperature together.
startBlizzard.title: Blizzard

startRain.description: Makes it rain. The intensity runs from a drizzle to a downpour.
startRain.title: Start rain

startStorm.description: Brings in a storm that lasts the given number of game hours.
startStorm.title: Start thunderstorm

stopRain.description: Stops the rain, leaving a running thunderstorm alone.
stopRain.title: Stop rain

stopWeather.description: Ends any running weather event and clears the sky.
stopWeather.title: Clear the weather

thunder.description: A thunderclap over a player. Left empty it picks a random one.
thunder.title: Thunder

triggerWeatherStage.description: Runs one of the game's own weather stages for a chosen duration — the same route the game's admin console takes.
triggerWeatherStage.title: Trigger a weather stage

events.apocalypseDay: Day {{day}} after the outbreak. A utility runs while that day is below its shut-off day.

categoryDescriptions.world: The frame the world runs in: time, date, daylight, view distance.
categoryDescriptions.zombies: Summon a horde or clear zombies. Everything here reaches deep.

deploy.adviceAllowlist: The platform knows your token but will not let it in. That is almost always the address list: in Coolify under Settings → Advanced, "Allowed API IPs" — add this panel’s own public address, or clear the field.
deploy.adviceGeneric: The platform refused without saying why. Its own log will say more than we can from here.
deploy.adviceMethod: The platform wants a different kind of request than the one sent. Update the panel — this is a fault on our side, not a setting on yours.
deploy.adviceNotConfigured: Enter the deploy webhook address first, then send a test.
deploy.advicePermission: The token is missing a permission. Create a new one under Keys & Tokens → API Tokens with "deploy" ticked, and paste it here.
deploy.advicePlatform: The platform answered with an error of its own. It is probably busy or mid-restart — look at its own log and try again.
deploy.adviceRateLimit: Too many requests for now. Coolify allows 200 an hour; wait a little and try again.
deploy.adviceToken: The token was not recognised. Check it was copied whole, and that it has not been revoked under Keys & Tokens → API Tokens.
deploy.adviceUnreachable: Nothing answered at that address. Check the panel can reach it: the hostname, the certificate, and whether the platform is running.
deploy.adviceUuid: Nothing was found at that address. The uuid in the webhook belongs to one application: copy it again from Automation → Webhooks of the application you mean.
deploy.allowlist: If "Allowed API IPs" is set, add this panel’s own address. The call comes from the machine the panel runs on, so your list can stay closed.
deploy.autoHint: As soon as a new version is available, it is deployed in your Coolify automatically.
deploy.description: When a new version is released, tell Coolify to fetch it. This replaces Coolify’s own "Automatic Deployment" switch, which watches a git repository and so never sees a release of this panel. Nothing happens unless you switch it on.
deploy.queuedHint: A deployment is queued. It does not mean the container is up yet — the version at the bottom left says when it is.
deploy.step1: In Coolify, open Settings → Advanced and switch API access on.
deploy.step2: Under Keys & Tokens → API Tokens, create a token with the deploy permission. Copy it now — it is shown once.
deploy.step3: Open your application, then Automation → Webhooks, and copy the topmost Deploy webhook. Not the GitHub or GitLab ones below it.
deploy.step4: Paste both here, send a test, then switch automatic deployment on.
deploy.title: Auto-deploy in Coolify
deploy.why: Your platform cannot see a new release on its own: this panel ships as an image, and a release changes no file it watches. So the panel tells it.
deploy.confirmTitle: Roll out the new version now?
deploy.confirmBody: Coolify pulls the current image and restarts the panel. That usually takes a minute or two, during which the panel is unreachable. This page reloads itself afterwards.

settings.description: Credentials that apply to the whole application.
settings.discordDescription: So the dashboard can talk to Discord. All three values are on the same application page in the Discord developer portal.
settings.discordInteractionUrl: Interactions Endpoint URL — this is what you paste into Discord:
settings.discordLocalUrl: This address is only reachable on this machine. Discord calls the dashboard from outside, so slash commands will not work until the dashboard is publicly reachable — notifications and chat to Discord do work already, because for those the dashboard calls Discord rather than the other way round.
settings.discordNextStep: After that, each game server is linked to its Discord server on its own "Discord" page.
settings.discordNote: Discord checks the address immediately and accepts it only once the public key is saved here. So save here first, then paste it into Discord.
settings.discordStep1: Create or open an application at discord.com/developers/applications.
settings.discordStep2: The application ID and public key are under "General Information".
settings.discordStep3: Generate the token under "Bot" — it is shown only once.
settings.discordStep4: Under "General Information", set the address below as the "Interactions Endpoint URL" and save.
settings.encryptionKeyDescription: Encrypts the stored FTP and RCON passwords.
settings.encryptionKeyOwnBody: This server uses the key from CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY. It is not shown here because you already have it — keep it separately from your database backups.
settings.encryptionKeyUnreadableBody: This server generated a key on first start, but the panel is not allowed to read the file. You will find it in the container at /app/var/secrets/credentials-key — save it from there.
settings.encryptionKeyWarnBody: It was generated on the first start and exists only in this container. Without it, a database backup restores everything except the FTP and RCON passwords. Copy it into your password manager.
settings.environmentHint: This value comes from an environment variable. Entering one here overrides it.
settings.googleDescription: Optional. Allows signing in with a Google account that has been linked to an existing login.
settings.googleNote: This address must match exactly, including scheme and path. It can only be changed in the Google Console, not here.

settings.googleStep1: Open the Google Cloud Console and create a project if you do not have one.
settings.googleStep2: Under Credentials, create an OAuth client ID of type Web application.
settings.googleStep3: Add the address below as an authorised redirect URI.

reason.dkimMissing: No key was found under the usual names. DKIM is set up at your mail provider, who gives you the record to publish.
reason.dmarcMissing: There is no DMARC record. Recipients do not know how to treat forged mail sent in your name.
reason.dmarcMonitorOnly: The record only monitors (“p=none”). That is the right starting point; tighten it to “quarantine” later.
reason.dmarcOk: The record is present and complete.
reason.dmarcPartialPercentage: Because of “pct” the record applies to only part of your mail. Remove “pct” so the rule covers all of it.
reason.spfMayNotCoverSender: The record does not name your mail server, so mail sent through this provider counts as unauthorised.
reason.spfMissing: There is no SPF record. Recipients cannot check whether the mail really came from you.
reason.spfNoAll: The record has no closing rule (“all”). Without it, what to do with unknown senders is left open.
reason.spfOk: The record is present and covers your mail server.
reason.spfPassAll: The record allows any server to send in your name with “+all”, which removes the protection entirely.
reason.spfUsesPtr: The record relies on “ptr”. That rule is deprecated and ignored by several large providers.
